alex kim: Heads-up — we're planning a KMS rotation next week (key alias: alias/siem-export-prod). Quick Q: will rotating break historical SIEM exports or stored archives that CI/CD unpacks for forensics?

maria chen: If we rotate without rewrapping, any objects encrypted with the old key will fail unwrap unless we keep DEK access. We currently use envelope encryption + a key-wrapping step in the export pipeline.

devon patel: Right — exports in GCS/S3 have metadata with `wrapped_key_id`. Rotation requires either rewrap of existing DEKs or a proxy that can unwrap old KEKs.

samira riley: Can we do a phased rotation? i.e., rotate the KEK, keep a short-lived service principal that can unwrap old DEKs for 30d, then re-encrypt older blobs during off-peak. That avoids a hard break.

alex kim: That sounds safe. Two follow-ups: 1) How does retention policy (we keep security logs 365d, long-term archive 7y) affect the rewrap work? 2) Any RBAC changes needed for oncall/forensics access during rotation?

maria chen: For retention: anything in the 7y bucket must be rewrapped eventually. Practically we'll target 0-365d in hot bucket first, then schedule batch rewraps for colder tiers. Estimate: ~3 TB/day rewrap throughput required to finish 7y in 2 weeks (rough calc).

devon patel: RBAC: create a scoped role `siem-key-rewraper` with temporary `kms:Decrypt`/`kms:Encrypt` on old/new KEKs, limited to the service account doing rewraps. Use a timebound grant via the access management system.

samira riley: Also log every rewrap op to the audit stream and tag with `rewrap-job-id`. We need to ensure SIEM ingests those audit events so reviewers can verify integrity.

security-bot: NOTICE: Planned KMS rotation scheduled 2026-06-03 02:00-06:00 UTC. Impact: rewrap required for historical SIEM archives encrypted with prior KEK. See runbook link: https://go/rundown/PRD-1234

oncall: If we need emergency access during rotation, use the JIT unmask flow (see playbook). Approvers: security-leads + eng-infra. Keep chatter in this thread and tag #incidents if we see failures.

alex kim: Ops checklist draft: 
```
- create `siem-key-rewraper` role (timebound)
- grant service principal temporary KMS unwrap/wrap
- run small smoke rewrap on 1 day of logs, validate SIEM import
- schedule bulk rewraps for hot then cold tiers
- stream rewrap audit events into SIEM channel
- update runbook + postmortem template
```

maria chen: One more: ensure any external SIEM consumers (partners/auditors) using exported snapshots can still decrypt. We should ship a compatibility notice and temporarily allow read-unwrapping via a proxy for approved consumer service accounts.

devon patel: I can put together the rewrap worker (k8s job) and add a `--dry-run` mode that emits audit events only. Will open RFC and a PR with scripts.

samira riley: Add a verification step: after rewrap, run hash compare + ingest test into staging SIEM to confirm nothing corrupted. Also add retention metadata update so old access tokens expire as expected.

alex kim: Great — action items: @devon open RFC+PR, @maria prepare IAM changelog and timeboxed grants, @samira add verification CI jobs, oncall to prep incident escalation channel. I'll schedule rotation window and post the external notice. :thumbsup:

security-bot: Event logged: ticket PRD-1234 created by alex kim. Expected owners: devon patel, maria chen, samira riley.

oncall: I'll standby during the window. If SIEM ingestion drops >5% we roll back and engage infra.

alex kim: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow for a dry-run.
